messages:
maria: Heads-up — new customer wants BYOK with HSM import. Need clarity on RBAC changes, audit retention, and incident response requirements before we sign the onboarding SOW. cc @devin @ashley

devin: Who exactly needs wrap/unwrap privileges vs just view/audit? My initial proposal: three roles — `kms-admin` (config, rotate policies), `key-operator` (import/wrap/unwrap under dual-op), `auditor` (read-only access to logs). Thoughts?

ashley: +1 on separation. For compliance we also need immutable audit exports and tamper-evidence. SOC2 + PCI customers will ask for 1y+ retention and provable integrity (signed bundles). Recommend forwarding HSM syslogs + KMS events to our SIEM and S3 with Object Lock (governance mode) for retention.

leo: Implementation note: our current HSM proxy supports single-operator imports only. For dual-operator we need peri-step manual witness or use an external threshold HSM (customer provides). If customer insists on dual-op, we'll need an ops play for physical handoffs or a vendor HSM that supports split KEK.

maria: Good catch. Can we get a short example of the minimal IAM/policy surface so legal understands scope? Also what's the incident path if an operator key is suspected compromised?

devin: Minimal policy example (very rough):
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:ImportKeyMaterial","kms:CreateKey"],"Resource":"arn:aws:kms:...:key/*","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"kms:role":"key-operator"}}},
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:Describe*","kms:GetKeyPolicy"],"Principal":{"AWS":["arn:aws:iam::123456:role/auditor"]}}
  ]
}
```
This keeps import/wrap ops scoped. We'll need an internal approval workflow around `kms:ImportKeyMaterial` (ticket + 2 approvers).

ashley: Incident path sketch: 1) Revoke operator entitlements immediately (RBAC rollback), 2) Quarantine affected key material if possible (HSM vendor), 3) Rotate/replace KEK and rewrap customer keys, 4) Notify customer + compliance per SLA, 5) Deliver signed audit bundle of actions. We should add automated alerts for anomalous `kms:ImportKeyMaterial` and multiple failed wrap attempts.

leo: On log capture: HSM syslogs -> syslog-ng -> SIEM; KMS control-plane events -> CloudTrail -> centralized bucket (Object Lock + SSE-KMS with a different CMK). CloudTrail filter for suspicious ops: `eventName = ImportKeyMaterial OR StartKeyDeletion OR ScheduleKeyDeletion`. Forward those to PagerDuty rule `sec-kms-signal`.

opsbot: deploy-bot: security-agent rule update deployed to staging: added CloudTrail -> SIEM connector and `ImportKeyMaterial` alert rule. CI/CD id: deploy-2024-11-78 :white_check_mark:

maria: Nice. Two outstanding questions for legal/compliance before we close: 1) retention window requirement (customer asked 3 years) — can we honor with Object Lock + export cadence? 2) Escrow/escrowless — do we permit customer-supplied HSM keys without escrow?

ashley: For 1) technically yes with Object Lock + periodic signed exports; need to confirm storage cost model for 3y retention. For 2) we can support both models, but escrowless (customer-only custody) needs contractual language about recovery limitations and incident notifications. Also require attestation of HSM firmware version and FIPS level.

maria: OK will surface to Legal + Sales. Action items: Devin to draft RBAC policy + approval workflow doc, Leo to write the log-forwarding runbook and dual-op gap doc, Ashley to draft incident response appendix and retention cost estimates. I'll open an onboarding ticket and link these items. Thanks all :thumbsup:
